Aditya Dwarkanath Sengupta And Ors vs The State Of
Maharashtra And Anr on 13 March, 2024

Author: A. S. Chandurkar
Bench: A. S. Chandurkar
2024:Bhc-As:12553-Db
 Sayyed 41-Wp(St)-19256-2
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Writ Petition (St) No.19256 Of 2023
 Aditya Dwarkanath Sengupta & Ors.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
..Petitioners
 Vs.
 The State of Maharashtra & Anr.

..Respondents
 __________
 Mr. Ganesh Bhujbal for the Petitioners.
Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 present in Court.
Mr. Ajay Patil, App for Respondent No.1 (State).
Mr. Ranjeet H. Patil for Respondent No.2.
Ms. Moumita Aditya Sengupta, Respondent No.2 present in Court.

_
 Coram : A. S. Chandurkar &
 Jitendra Jain, Jj.
Date : 13th March 2024.

The present Writ Petition has been filed seeking quashing of First Information Report No.498 of
2022 that has thereafter resulted into registration of Regular Criminal Case No.1838 of 2023 under
Sections 498A, 420, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
During the pendency of the Writ Petition, the Petitioner No.3 has expired.
The learned counsel for the Petitioners has placed on record death certificate which is taken on record and marked "A" for identification.

3. It is informed by the learned counsel for the parties that the Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and Respondent No.2 have decided to give an 1 of 2 Sayyed 41-WP(ST)-19256-2023.doc end to the disputes between the parties.
An affidavit on behalf of the Respondent No.2 is filed in support thereof.

It has been agreed that the parties would file a joint petition for divorce by mutual consent before the Family Court and subject to the same and other agreed terms, the dispute would be put to Aditya Dwarkanath Sengupta And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53120427/

entities.text: Aditya Dwarkanath Sengupta And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 an end.
The Petitioners as well as Respondent No.2 are present in Court today and they accept the fact that the proceedings are sought to be put to an end.

4. Considering the fact that the registration of the First Information Report has its genesis in the matrimonial dispute and parties have now agreed to put an end to the same on agreed terms and conditions, we are inclined to quash the proceedings since no useful purpose would be served by continuing the same.
A case has thus been made out to exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
5. In view of the aforesaid, the proceedings arising out of First Information Report No.498 of 2022 that has resulted in RCC No.1838 of 2023, the same stands quashed as being mutually settled.
The writ petition in allowed in terms of prayer clause (a) subject to the parties acting in accordance with the agreed terms.
6. Order accordingly.
(JITENDRA JAIN, J.) (A. S. CHANDURKAR, J.) Signed by: Sayyed Saeed Ali 2 of 2 Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 15/03/2024 15:07:59
